title: Eval: cost vs regression thresholds and cheap-config gating
content:
Purpose:

This is a working note for defining a defensible, auditable rule-set that ties automated quality gates (on our eval suites) to the set of lower-cost serving configurations we will allow in production for a given model+workload. The goal: avoid silent quality regressions while unlocking predictable unit-cost savings via quantization, smaller model variants, and aggressive batching/caching.

Background / motivation:
- We have multiple levers to reduce token/unit cost: int8/int4 quantization, smaller model checkpoints (e.g., 13B -> 7B), aggressive KV/prefix cache settings, and larger batch sizes on Dedicated.
- Engineering and finance want a principled way to permit these cheaper configs for customers without manual review every time.
- Current practice is ad hoc: experiments live in PRs, and rollouts sometimes cause small but customer-visible quality drops. We need a reproducible gate that: (a) ties to eval metrics, (b) quantifies cost delta, and (c) recommends auto-fallback/rollback thresholds.

Key definitions (how we’ll talk about things here):
- baseline: production model configuration we consider the reference quality (usually fp16 or our current deployment).
- cheap-config: any change that decreases expected cost per token by > 3% (examples: 8-bit quant, smaller variant, larger batching).
- eval suite: curated dataset for a workload (generation prompts, chat flows, retrieval+rerank, embeddings) with pass/fail metrics.
- quality regression: reduction in primary metric(s) beyond an allowed delta compared to baseline.
- cost uplift / delta: expected change in cost-per-inference or cost-per-1M tokens estimated by the spreadsheet model.

High-level proposal:
1) For each workload, maintain an "Eval Profile" spreadsheet with: baseline metrics, lower-cost candidate configs, expected cost delta, and per-metric deltas. This is the control document used for gating.
2) Define a two-tier gate system: 
   - Soft gate (auto-approve): candidate config can be enabled automatically if:
     * primary metric delta <= T_soft (e.g., <= 0.5% absolute or relative depending on metric), AND
     * secondary metrics within S_soft, AND
     * expected cost delta >= C_min (e.g., >= 5% savings), AND
     * observed variance across n=3 runs within tolerance.
   - Hard gate (manual review required): any candidate failing the soft gate but with expected cost delta >= C_min goes to product/ML review.
3) A configuration that passes the soft gate will be placed into a canary rollout with metric monitoring hooks and a rollback timer (48h). If live monitoring shows drift beyond run-time thresholds, immediate rollback occurs.

Choosing thresholds (concrete heuristics):
- Primary metric thresholds should depend on metric type. Example heuristics: 
  * classification accuracy / exact match: T_soft = 0.5% absolute; T_hard = 1.5% absolute
  * F1/Rouge: T_soft = 0.7% relative; T_hard = 2.0% relative
  * embeddings cosine/semantic-qa NDCG: T_soft = 0.3% absolute; T_hard = 1.0% absolute
  * human-eval / preference win-rate: T_soft = 2.5% relative; T_hard = 5% relative
- Cost cutoff C_min is set contextually; suggested default = 5% for hosted API, 8% for Dedicated (since Dedicated customers value predictability).
- Minimum statistical power: each eval must have enough samples to detect the soft threshold with p >= 0.8 assuming observed variance; default sample sizes are in the spreadsheet.

Spreadsheet model notes (how to estimate cost delta):
- Inputs: tokens per request distribution (p25/p50/p75), baseline latency and throughput, target hardware price/slot-hour, batching assumptions, KV/cache hit rate, quantization efficiency multiplier (e.g., int8 CPU/GPU factor), and pre/post-processing overheads.
- Outputs: expected $/1M tokens, 99th-pct latency delta, throughput delta, and projected monthly savings for N users or QPS.
- Important: separate token-cost from infra-fixed costs. Some cheaper configs increase latency or reduce throughput which can increase infra cost at scale; gating must account for that tradeoff (we prefer unit-cost > infra-cost reduction).

Evaluation design (practical blueprint):
1) Create a copy of the Eval Profile spreadsheet for the workload (linked artifact).
2) Run baseline and each cheap-config on the curated eval suite with n=3 independent runs (random seeds, sampling different prompt shuffles when applicable).
3) Record: primary and secondary metrics, standard deviation, time/latency statistics, cost-model inputs (tokens, avg latency), and the estimated $ delta.
4) Run lightweight human spot-checks on ~100 samples for any config that is near a soft threshold (within 20% of T_soft) to catch qualitative failure modes not in metrics.
5) Produce a gating recommendation row in the spreadsheet: PASS_SOFT, REVIEW_HARD, REJECT.

Automation & rollout integration:
- A pipeline job will: given a PR that proposes a cheap-config, run the eval suite, auto-fill the Eval Profile sheet, and label the PR with PASS_SOFT / REVIEW_HARD / REJECT.
- For PASS_SOFT: pipeline triggers canary rollout via the deployment system and posts monitoring links to the PR.
- For REVIEW_HARD: notify product and ML leads with a short summary (metric deltas, cost delta, examples).

Monitoring signals to watch in canary (live):
- Primary metric delta compared to baseline (rolling window 1h, 24h).
- Error rate/aborts per 1k requests.
- Latency P90/P99 and token throughput.
- Qualitative Slack reports from CS/SEs tagging anomalies.

Open design questions and risks:
- Multi-metric tradeoffs: For complex workloads (e.g., summarization where ROUGE declines but latency improves), how to weigh metrics? Proposal: define a weighted score per workload maintained in the Eval Profile; changes in weighted score map to gates. Need product sign-off per workload.
- Dataset representativeness: our eval suites often under-represent long-tail cases. Consider periodic adversarial sampling and expanding the human-check sample.
- Cost estimation variance: cloud price changes and actual load patterns can change realized savings. Require a quarterly review of the cost model assumptions and a conservative buffer on C_min.
- Customer-facing configurations: for Dedicated customers we should not auto-apply cheap-configs without explicit customer opt-in; gating is internal recommendation only.

Action items (owners & timeline):
- Priya: finalize Eval Profile spreadsheet template and column definitions. Due 2026-03-06. (sheet link in linked_artifacts)
- Marco: implement evaluation runner that writes results into the sheet and computes pass/fail logic. Prototype by 2026-03-20.
- Sofia: define weighted-score rubric for 4 vertical workloads (search, summarization, chat, embeddings). Draft by 2026-03-13.
- Avery: wire canary monitoring alerts and rollback automation; ensure PR auto-labeler integration. Proof-of-concept by 2026-04-01.
- Jordan: run a retrospective on the last 3 rollouts that used quantization and document what we missed. Due 2026-03-10.

Notes to reviewers:
- This draft intentionally biases towards conservative thresholds for soft gates to build trust in automation. We expect thresholds to loosen once the pipelines and monitoring mature.
- Please review the sample-size table in the spreadsheet (linked) — it's the most consequential component for whether small deltas are detectable.

Appendix: quick worked example (toy):
- Baseline: 13B fp16, hosted API, $0.80 / 1M tokens (toy)
- Cheap-config A: 13B int8, estimated runtime multiplier 0.65, expected cost = $0.52 / 1M tokens (35% savings)
- Eval result: accuracy -0.35% absolute, rouge -0.6% relative, embeddings NDCG -0.1% absolute
- Apply heuristics: accuracy delta (0.35) <= T_soft (0.5) -> pass, rouge delta (0.6) slightly > T_soft (0.7 relative threshold maps to 0.7) -> pass, cost delta 35% >= C_min (5%) -> pass -> PASS_SOFT -> schedule canary rollout 48h with monitoring.

Questions for next meeting:
- Do we want separate C_min thresholds for embeddings vs generation? (I lean yes; embeddings are more sensitive to small vector drift.)
- How aggressive do Legal/Compliance teams want us to be on customer opt-in for Dedicated?
- Which team maintains the canonical Eval Profile spreadsheets? Suggest product-optimize with read access to SRE and ML teams.
